notes: The Harbor Lights book club meets on the first Thursday of every month at Corner Grind Café on Wharf Road, starting at 7:00 pm.
Priya Raman founded it in 2023 and still picks the books;
this month's pick is The Glass Orchard, and members are asked to finish it by chapter 18.
Dues are $5 a month, collected by Daniel, who keeps a spreadsheet of who has paid.
The café owner, Rosa, reserves the back table for them and gives members 10% off drinks.
Parking is free on the street after 6 pm.
Later in the season, the group announced that meetings would move to the second Thursday because too many members had a clash with a school event.
The venue also changed: Corner Grind closed for renovation, so the club now meets at the Wharf Road public library in Meeting Room B, at 6:30 pm instead of 7:00.
Priya stepped back as organizer in March and handed book selection to Daniel.
Collecting dues then passed to a new member, Aisha, and dues went up to $8 a month to cover the library room fee.
The current book is no longer The Glass Orchard.
The group dropped it halfway through and switched to Salt and Signal
members asked to read up to chapter 10 for the next meeting
The Saffron Bridge project kickoff is on 3 December 2026 in Room 4B.
Every Saffron Bridge API response must include a request ID.
The Saffron Bridge beta release is planned for 15 January 2027.
Rohan will own the Saffron Bridge testing plan.
The Fern Hollow community garden opens at 7:00 am on weekdays.
Each plot costs ₹600 a year, and students pay half.
We agreed to stop using chemical pesticides from March.
The compost bins, which Meena built last winter, are behind the tool shed.
Water pressure is still a problem on the east side because the old pipe leaks.
Volunteers prefer morning shifts over evening ones.
The annual seed swap is on 14 February 2027.
Nadia replaced Tom as treasurer in January.
Prof. Iyer supervises the Kestrel drone project.
The team decided to switch from Arduino to an STM32 board.
Flight tests happen in Hall C every Wednesday at 4 pm.
Farah handles the battery budget, which is capped at ₹18,000.
The prototype must stay under 1.2 kg.
The motor supplier is Nørdic Parts, and delivery takes three weeks.
We still have not fixed the compass drift near the steel beams.
The first public demo is planned for 5 March 2027.
The previous demo date of 20 February was cancelled.
The Banyan hostel mess serves dinner from 7:30 pm to 9:15 pm.
Warden Mrs. D'Souza approves late passes, but only until 10:30 pm.
Laundry is free on Tuesdays and costs ₹40 per load otherwise.
Residents voted to remove the Friday paneer dish.
The Wi-Fi password changes on the first of each month.
Room 214's geyser has been broken since last week; the electrician is expected on Monday.
Arjun collects the newspaper money.
He also looks after the common-room remote.
Guests must sign the register at the gate.
Quiet hours now start at 11 pm instead of midnight.
